episode.title: Strip truncated tool-argument markup glued to a bare tool name
episode.before: At parent commit 41c17d9b5e1299b404700f86d6abad5cd406f3b6, the unterminated-tool-call sanitizer recognized argument tags only when the tag itself began the line, or when an argument closer ended the line. A truncated serialization such as `process_manage<arg_key>action</arg_key>...` therefore retained raw tool-contract markup because the bare tool name preceded the first argument tag.
episode.after: At cf8b08edac3a78feb4b9db0c20a62934c3a6c49d, the sanitizer accepts an optional identifier-only prefix composed of word characters, dots, colons, or hyphens before a line-boundary argument tag. Consequently, bare-name-prefixed truncated calls are removed from both display and stored-visible text, while prose containing a space before an argument-tag example remains outside the match.
episode.diff: The change replaces the argument-fragment branch `[ \t]*</?arg_...` with `[ \t]*[\w.:-]*</?arg_...` in the shared unterminated-tool-call regular expression and updates its boundary rationale. Two parameterized regression cases cover a complete bare-name-prefixed fragment and one cut during its argument value; the existing parameterization runs both display and storage sanitizers and retains prose-preservation coverage.

evidence_units.claim: Commit cf8b08edac3a78feb4b9db0c20a62934c3a6c49d has parent 41c17d9b5e1299b404700f86d6abad5cd406f3b6 and describes raw markup leaking when a cut call has no opener and its bare tool name shares a line with `<arg_key>`.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller cf8b08edac3a78feb4b9db0c20a62934c3a6c49d; issue-bundle.json linked pull request 101899

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation requires an argument tag to follow line-leading whitespace directly: `(?:^|\n)[ \t]*</?arg_(?:key|value)\b[^\n]*`. It therefore does not recognize a bare name immediately before the tag.
The patch inserts `[\w.:-]*` between line-leading whitespace and the argument tag, permitting a no-space identifier-like prefix while excluding ordinary spaced prose.
The updated pattern belongs to `_THINK_STRIP_PATTERNS`; `strip_think_blocks` applies every pattern in that collection by substitution to produce visible text.
The regression test applies every cut-fragment case to two sanitization paths: the final-display `_strip_reasoning_tags` path and the storage-visible `strip_think_blocks` path.
New cases require `Done.\nprocess_manage<arg_key>action</arg_key><arg_value>wait</arg_value>` to become `Done.` and `Hi.\nterminal<arg_key>command</arg_key><arg_value>ls -la` to become `Hi.`.
Existing negative coverage requires lines such as `The <arg_key> holds the parameter name.` and their surrounding prose to survive unchanged for both sanitizers.

A direct Python behavioral probe comparing the parent and patched expressions confirmed that the parent misses both new fragment shapes, the patched expression removes both, and the patched expression preserves the spaced inline-prose example.
evidence_units.source: Local python3 probe executed against the exact parent and patched regular-expression branches during extraction; result: `PASS: patched regex removes both bare-name-prefixed fragments and preserves inline prose`

evidence_units.claim: Only the shared runtime sanitizer and its focused CLI/storage regression test file changed: 8 insertions and 4 deletions across two files.
The implementation comment defines the safety boundary: the optional prefix represents a bare tool name with no spaces, so inline prose such as `The <arg_key> holds...` must survive.

candidate_atomics.name: strip-bare-name-prefixed-tool-fragments
candidate_atomics.description: Recognize and remove an unrecoverable, line-boundary tool-argument fragment when its first argument tag is glued to an identifier-like tool name, without treating spaced prose as structured output.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent truncated structured tool-call markup from leaking into user-visible or stored assistant text while retaining unrelated natural-language content.
semantic_action.module_role: Shared assistant-text sanitization boundary for structured reasoning and tool-call artifacts.
semantic_action.pre_state: A sanitizer already removes unterminated argument-tag fragments beginning directly at a line boundary, but a truncated fragment whose first tag is immediately preceded by a bare identifier-like tool name remains visible.
semantic_action.post_state: At a line boundary, an optional no-space identifier-like prefix followed by an argument tag is classified as an unrecoverable tool fragment and removed; spaced prose mentioning an argument tag remains unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Run the same fragment cases through both display and storage sanitizers, assert the visible prefix remains and the structured suffix disappears, then assert spaced inline tag prose and following text survive unchanged.

candidate_workflows.name: repair-truncated-structured-output-sanitization
candidate_workflows.description: Tighten a structured-output sanitizer around one observed truncated serialization shape, using a constrained prefix grammar and paired positive and negative regression checks.

workflow_graph.goal: Remove bare-name-prefixed truncated tool-argument markup from every visible-text sanitization path without broadening the match into ordinary prose.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A stream can end after emitting a bare tool name and argument markup but before producing a recoverable complete tool-call block; current line-boundary recognition misses that shape.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Display and storage sanitizers remove the newly identified fragment shapes, preserve preceding visible text, and leave spaced inline prose examples intact.
